title: Account deletion with a grace period

requirements.text: A signed-in user (re-authenticated) can request deletion of their account
Deletion is scheduled after a configurable grace period, during which the account is disabled
The user can cancel during the grace period and regain access
Existing sessions and tokens are revoked when deletion is requested
Dependent data is deleted, anonymized or retained per a declared policy when the period ends
Only the account owner (or an authorized admin) can request or cancel deletion
The scheduled deletion runs once, survives retries and records completion

evidence.name: request requires a signed-in, recently re-authenticated owner
grace period: deletion is scheduled graceMs later and the account is disabled meanwhile
cancel during the grace period restores access
schema applies and the SQL store keeps request, cancel, grace and completion behavior
sessions are revoked on request; a failed revocation schedules nothing
dependent data is deleted, anonymized or retained per the declared policy
authorization: only the owner or an authorized admin can request, cancel or read
idempotent execution: runs once, retries resume after a failed step and completion is recorded
two concurrent runDue calls claim and execute each due account exactly once
a crashed run resumes after the lease expires and skips completed steps
lease renewal: a queued request whose lease expired is skipped
lease renewal on PostgreSQL: a queued request whose lease expired is skipped

notes: module:account-deletion covers the workflow with injected authorize, revokeSessions and policy handlers; tests use an in-memory store and PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite. PGlite is a single connection, so the concurrent runDue evidence proves the single conditional claim UPDATE when statements interleave, not behavior under real multi-connection contention; lease renewal before each request and handler is tested on both stores. The application still implements and tests each data handler against its real tables (including a second run), the sign-in gate (isDisabled) and deletion outside its database (backups, logs, processors). durable-jobs can schedule runDue.
